policy: Declaration-only intended Belgian gate posture. Belgium has no incumbent dataset, so incumbent-comparison gates (parity, export_surface, target_surface) are not selected. National and NUTS1 references are declared release-blocking and commune-grain references diagnostic, but this schema change does not wire target-profile tiers or roles into runtime gates. External-oracle implementation (EUROMOD-BE baselines and Federal Planning Bureau reform scores) remains separate work in #264 and is not implemented here.

gates.notes: Calibration fit per source family (demography, fiscal income, income tax, social security, caseloads) so no family hides in the average.

Intended weighted aggregates against admin anchors on the future hard surface. The tier metadata in target_references.json is declaration-only in this change; a later runner integration must explicitly bridge it into gate tolerances.
Commune-grain diagnostics render per-target fit with the worst-fit communes named; promotion to release_blocking is a spine-quality decision (populace#263), not a default.
The eventual active target profile must cover every named family; the schema declarations and placeholders in this change do not themselves activate that surface.
The US demographics.json / base_population_scale posture against Statbel population structure: age-band x sex x region totals within tight tolerance.
No all-zero stored layers: an all-zero column is a pipeline bug or dead scaffolding masking engine defaults.

No Axiom derived-rule output may persist as a dataset input (a stored engine output masks reforms) — enforced from day one; the adapter's writer refuses such columns and this gate re-checks the artifact.
Physically non-negative columns (incomes, contributions) carry no negatives; the column list follows the source manifest's nonnegative_outputs.
Broad release-blocking band against the NBB household-sector anchor — a levels sanity check, not a calibration target (the populace#212 lesson).
